sub: Warm questions — built so someone actually feels heard.

1.name: Open
q: Say a small thing that happened today you haven't told anyone yet.~They ask one follow-up. You answer it properly.
What's something you're quietly proud of this week that nobody's asked about?
Guess a rule I live by that I've never said out loud.~Then I tell you mine, and you say whether it sounds like me.
Guess what people assume about me that's just wrong.~Then I tell you what I'd assumed about you, and you correct me.
Name someone who believed in you before you believed in yourself.~Then they ask what that person saw. Answer as though you believe it.
What's a smell, sound, or texture that calms you down almost instantly?
Say a small kindness from a stranger you still think about.~After they answer, tell them what it says about what they notice.
Name one thing about the person across from you that you already like.~They aren't allowed to deflect it for ten seconds.
Guess the most useless skill I'm secretly excellent at.~Then I demonstrate it, badly, right now.
Say an opinion that would surprise the people who think they know you best.~Then they guess which of your friends would be most surprised.
When's the last time you laughed so hard it actually hurt?
Name a small thing you do for other people that you don't think they've noticed.~After they answer, tell them you noticed something like it tonight — and what.
What's the best advice you've ever ignored, on purpose?
On three, both say the first thing you notice walking into any room.~Different answers tell you what each of you is scanning for.
Guess something I was sure I'd hate and turned out to love.~Then I tell you, and you say whether it fits.
Who did something for you this week that you still haven't thanked them for?
Name a small thing you've never grown out of and don't want to.~After they answer, tell them not to grow out of it. Mean it.
Guess what they're better at than they let on.~Then they have to admit they're good at it, out loud, with no hedging.
What's the boldest thing on your bucket list that you actually intend to do?
Say a small tradition that's just yours — nobody else knows you keep it.~They ask one question about it. You answer properly.
If tonight had a soundtrack, play ten seconds of the first song.~They rate the choice out of ten and have to justify the score.
What's a moment this year that felt like it belonged in a movie, with you in the lead?
What's the last thing you searched that says way too much about your week?
Guess what I order without even looking at the menu.~Then I tell you — and you're ordering for me next time. That's binding.
What's a small superstition you secretly follow, even though you know it's silly?
Say the last thing that made you laugh out loud completely alone.~Then show them, if you can find it. No explaining first.
What's a food combination you love that everyone else thinks is a crime?
Guess what I'm weirdly, unnecessarily competitive about.~Then we settle it right now, badly, at this table.
Name a compliment someone gave you once that you still carry around.~After they answer, tell them whether you'd have said the same thing.
What's the most impulsive good decision you've ever made?
What's a movie or show you could rewatch forever and never get tired of?
Say a nickname you've had — good, bad, or humiliating.~They pick which one they're using for the rest of the night. No appeals.
What's the best gift you've ever given someone, and how'd you land on it?
What's something you collect, on purpose or completely by accident?
What's a place you've never been that you think about more than you'd expect?
Free flight tomorrow, your name on it. Say the destination, no thinking.~Then they guess why that one, and you say how close they got.
What's a small habit you'd probably deny having unless someone asked you straight out?
What's the strangest job you've ever done, even just for a day?
What's a phrase or saying you picked up from someone and never put down?
Say your actual karaoke song — the one you'd pick, not the one you'd claim.~Then play five seconds of it. They judge how honest the answer was.
Guess what makes me trust a stranger almost instantly.~Then I tell you whether you've done it tonight.

2.name: Deeper
q: Name who you wish you told 'thank you' or 'I love you' to more often.~After they answer, ask what's actually stopping them. Don't accept 'no reason'.
Guess a fear I've gone quieter about as I've got older.~Then I tell you, and you say whether you'd have known.
Say something you needed to hear when you were younger that nobody said.~After they answer, say it to them now. Properly, like you mean it.
Say what you do quietly when you're trying to feel better and no one's watching.~They don't comment. They listen to the whole thing.
What's a memory that still gets you, every time you think about it?
Home — a place or a person, right now? Pick one. 'Both' isn't an answer.~Then they ask why that one, and you answer straight.
Guess when they feel lonely, even around people.~Then they tell you. Get it wrong and ask properly.
Name the gap between who you are and who people think you are.~After they answer, tell them which version you've been talking to tonight.
Guess the version of themselves they're glad they outgrew.~Then they tell you, and you say what you'd have kept.
Say something you're proud of that would never make it onto a resume.~After they answer, tell them why it's the more impressive one.
What's a belief about yourself you're slowly trying to let go of?
On three, both say what you needed more of growing up — attention, space, praise, or quiet.~Then say whether you get enough of it now.
When did you last genuinely surprise yourself?
Guess how I've changed since eighteen in a way that'd surprise people who knew me then.~Then I tell you, and you say which version you'd have preferred.
What's something you do to feel in control when everything else isn't?
Tell a family story that explains more about you than you'd like it to.~They ask one follow-up. You don't get to pick which one.
What's the real difference between the version of you new people meet and the version you actually are?
Name something you've forgiven someone for but never actually told them.~After they answer, ask whether telling them would change anything.
Guess a small ache they carry that most people wouldn't guess is there.~Wrong is the good outcome here. Then ask properly.
Say something you keep almost telling people and then don't.~Say it now instead. They aren't allowed to interrupt.
Who's someone you've drifted from that you still think about?
Guess how they show love in a way people might not clock as love.~Then they tell you, and you say whether you've seen them do it tonight.
What's something you privately worry might be true about you?
Say what you wish someone would just notice without you having to say it.~After they answer, tell them one thing you have noticed, unprompted.
What's something about who you are that you're still figuring out, even now?
What's a piece of advice you give other people but can't quite take yourself?
Name the last time you felt truly safe with someone — not physically, just safe.~Then they ask what made it safe. Be specific.
Guess something I pretend doesn't bother me but actually does.~Then I confirm or correct it. No pretending either way.
What's a question people used to ask you that you wish they still would?
What's something you're grieving that isn't a death — a plan, a version of life, a person who's still around?
Say the kindest thing you could say to yourself right now that you haven't.~Then they say it back to you, in their own voice, and you have to take it.
What's something you've gotten better at hiding instead of actually healing?
Name who you'd call at 3am without hesitating.~Then they ask how long that list is. Answer honestly, however short it is.
Say what you're quietly waiting for permission to do, though no one's stopping you.~After they answer, give them the permission. Out loud, properly.
What's a way you've let yourself down that you haven't quite forgiven yet?
What's something you never really let yourself fall apart over, even though you probably needed to?
Name a part of your life that looks fine from the outside but doesn't always feel it.~They just listen. No advice, no fixing, no silver lining.
What's something you wish you could unlearn about how relationships are supposed to work?
What's a moment someone saw the real you before you were ready for it?
Guess something they're scared they might want too much.~Then they tell you, and neither of you makes it smaller than it is.
Say a way you protect yourself that might also be keeping the right people out.~After they answer, tell them whether you've felt it tonight. Gently, but honestly.

3.name: Close
q: Say one true thing about yourself, out loud, that you don't say very often.
Look at them. Don't say anything for a second. Then tell them what you see.
What's something you've never told anyone because you thought it'd change how they saw you?
Finish this out loud, to them — 'Something I appreciate about you that I don't think I've said is…'
What's a moment — tonight, this week, or in your life — you'd call sacred, if you let yourself use that word?
What do you hope they remember about tonight — not what you said, but how you made them feel?
Tell them one thing you've noticed about them tonight that you haven't said out loud yet. Let them just take it in before you say anything else.
When did you last cry in front of someone?
What's something about tonight you already know you don't want to forget?
If tonight was the only night you ever got to know this person, what would you make sure they knew?
What's the truest compliment anyone could give you — the one that would actually land, not just sound nice?
What does it feel like, right now, to be looked at like this?
What's something you're still a little afraid to want?~After they answer, tell them the one part that actually stayed with you.
What's something you still wish someone would just say to you?~Once they've answered, say it to them — for real, like you mean it.
What do you think people get wrong about you?~Once they've answered, tell them what you actually see instead — the true version.
What's a fear about the future you don't usually say out loud?~After they answer, tell them one reason you think they'll be okay anyway.
What's a compliment you've never fully believed, even when someone meant it?~After they answer, tell them exactly why you believe it's true.
Is there something you're proud of that's never really been given the credit it deserves?~After they answer, give them the credit — specifically, out loud.
When have you felt invisible, even around people who were supposed to know you?~After they answer, tell them one specific way you see them right now.
What's something about yourself that's taken you the longest to forgive?~After they answer, tell them: if you'd been in their shoes, you'd forgive them for it in a heartbeat.
What's a version of 'I love you' you find easier to show than to say?~After they answer, tell them you've noticed — and when.
What's something you once needed someone to fight for, and nobody did?~After they answer, tell them: you would have.
What's a question about yourself you're honestly afraid of the answer to?~You don't have to answer it tonight — just tell them what the question is, and let it sit there between you.
When did you last feel proud of who you are, not just what you did?~After they answer, tell them: that's exactly who you've been sitting across from tonight.
What's true about how you're feeling right now, in this exact second, that you haven't said out loud?
What's something you're only now realizing about yourself, right in this conversation?
What's the bravest thing about how you've shown up tonight?
Say the thing you'd say if you knew, for certain, it wouldn't scare them off.
What do you notice in your body right now, after everything you've just said tonight?
What's something about tonight that's made you see them differently than you did an hour ago?
What's true about you tonight that wouldn't have been true a year ago?
What's a feeling you're having right now that you're tempted to downplay?
What's something you've never said to someone you loved because the timing never felt right?~After they answer, ask them: is there a version of it you could say out loud tonight — to anyone?
What's a wound that's mostly healed but still aches on the right day?~After they answer, ask what helps on those days — and tell them you'll remember it.
What's something you did once that still quietly embarrasses you, even though nobody else remembers it?~After they answer, tell them: that's not who you see sitting across from you.
What's a part of yourself you're only now starting to actually like?~After they answer, tell them one thing you already liked about it before they said anything.
What's something you needed to hear from a parent that you're still waiting on?~After they answer, say the thing to them — as if you were the one who should've said it.
What's the loneliest you've ever felt while surrounded by people who loved you?~After they answer, tell them: you're not in that room right now.
What's something you're carrying tonight that you didn't expect to bring up?~You don't have to explain it fully — just name it, and let them sit in it with you.
What's a version of the future you're quietly hoping for, even if you'd never bet on it out loud?~After they answer, ask them what the very first sign of it coming true might look like.

wild: Hold eye contact for ten seconds. No talking. Then say the first word that comes to you.
Give them a genuine compliment — the kind you'd usually keep to yourself.
Sit in silence together for fifteen seconds. Actually notice what that feels like.
Point at something they're wearing, carrying, or holding, and ask for the real story behind it.
Trade a small secret. Nothing dramatic — just something true. You go first.
Play the song that matches this exact moment. No explaining it, just play it.
Describe the person across from you to a stranger, in one sentence.
Finish this out loud: 'What I'm not saying is…'
Talk for sixty seconds straight about whatever's actually on your mind. They just listen — no jumping in, no fixing it, not even a question until the minute's up.
Name three actual, specific things you're grateful this person did, said, or is. No deflecting with a joke.
After their next answer, say back what you actually heard before you reply with your own. Not 'same' — the real thing, in your own words.
Raise whatever's in your hand and give them an actual, specific toast. Not 'cheers' — a real one, out loud.
Both say one true thing about yourselves you don't say often — but you have to look at each other the whole time, not the table.
Ask them one question you've been curious about all night but haven't asked yet.
Switch seats, or scoot closer than you started. Notice if anything shifts.
Ask them to teach you one thing they know how to do — right now, in one sentence.
Hold their hand for five seconds. No talking. Just that.
Mirror their posture for the next thirty seconds without telling them why.
Ask them what they need to hear right now — then actually say it, out loud.
Ask them to describe you in exactly three words — no hedging, no take-backs.
final: Look at each other properly for a second — not mid-sentence, not through a screen. Just look.
Each of you, out loud: one specific thing about tonight — or about them — you don't want to forget.
Say thank you for it, plainly, no joke to hide behind. And mean it.
